claims.label: Purpose
claims.excerpt:
Glow is a terminal based markdown reader designed from the ground up to bring
out the beauty—and power—of the CLI.

Use it to discover markdown files, read documentation directly on the command
line. Glow will find local markdown files in subdirectories or a local
Git repository.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body:
A representative use is piping Markdown text into `glow`. In `main.go`, `execute` checks whether stdin is a pipe; when it is, it wraps stdin in a source and calls `executeCLI` with stdout as the destination.

`executeCLI` reads the entire source into memory and passes those bytes through `utils.RemoveFrontmatter`. It then constructs a Glamour terminal renderer with a selected style, word-wrap width, base URL, and preserved-newline option.

Before rendering, the CLI checks `utils.IsMarkdownFile(src.URL)`. If that check marks the source as code, it wraps the text in a code block using the source extension. It passes the resulting content to `r.Render`, returns a contextual error on failure, and passes successful output through `utils.ApplyTextSizing`.

With neither alternate display mode selected, the result is rendered text written to stdout—not the original input bytes. The default branch prints `out` to the supplied writer and reports an error if the write fails.

sections.title: A closer look
sections.body:
A useful design choice is that output adapts to its destination: validation tests whether stdout is a terminal and chooses the `notty` style when it is not, unless the style flag was explicitly changed. That style is then passed into renderer construction.

Wrapping is terminal-aware too. When no width flag was changed and the configured width is zero, validation tries to obtain the terminal width, caps the detected value at 120, and falls back to 80 if width remains zero. Renderer construction receives that width as its word-wrap setting.

sections.title: Where to look next
sections.body: To explore customization next, start with the style and width flags in `main.go`. To follow the interactive alternative, start at `runTUI`: it copies display settings into a UI configuration, calls `ui.NewProgram(cfg, content)`, and runs the returned program. That is the handoff beyond the CLI path described here.

	cfg.Path = path

	cfg.ShowLineNumbers = showLineNumbers

	prog, cleanup := ui.NewProgram(cfg, content)
	defer cleanup()
